# KANCITY
### Film / Limited Series Treatment — Based on True Events
**Status:** Part 1 of an ongoing account. Additional installments to be added as the story continues.

---

## LOGLINE (draft — to be refined as more of the story is added)

A freshman arrives on campus full of hope and ambition, only to have a single lost wallet pull him into the orbit of the region's most feared confraternity — and into a relationship with its executioner that will threaten everything he came there to build.

---

## FORMAT & GENRE

Based on true events. Coming-of-age / crime drama with elements of psychological thriller. Told from the protagonist's first-person perspective, tracing his slow, almost accidental descent into a world he never intended to enter.

---

## SYNOPSIS (Part 1)

**KAN** arrives on campus for the first time, buzzing with excitement. He is the last among his friend group to gain admission, and stepping onto the grounds finally feels like catching up — like he belongs.

That excitement doesn't last.

Kan loses his wallet — cash, and a slip of paper with his friend's phone number, the only real anchor he has back home. He doesn't even realize it's gone until his friend calls: a group of strangers has been in touch, saying they have it. They pass along a number.

Kan is new. He hasn't left the hostel grounds since he arrived — he doesn't know the streets, doesn't know who's out there. But the wallet has money in it, so after lectures he calls the number. A voice tells him to come outside the school premises to collect it.

At 5 p.m., he does.

He finds a group of more than seven men, seated, drinking. They wave him over, offer him a seat. He takes it. They tell him to drink with them. He says no — and the mood turns, fast enough that he understands the "no" isn't really an option. He drinks.

Eventually he tries to leave, telling them he has to get back to his hostel. This is the moment — though Kan doesn't know it yet — that marks the beginning of his entanglement with the **Viking Confraternity**, widely regarded as the most feared cult group in the state, and one of the deadliest in the country.

Unknown to Kan, one of the men at that table is the group's serving **executioner** — a title, and a role, that carries real weight in that world. We'll call him **EMK**.

Throughout the encounter, Kan notices a pattern: other rough-looking men drift by to greet the group, but when they greet EMK specifically, they use both hands — a small gesture, but a loaded one. Status. Deference. Fear, maybe.

As Kan grows visibly restless to leave, EMK's demeanor shifts. He starts asking Kan about his studies — almost fatherly, almost kind. Before Kan goes, EMK gives him his personal number, tells him to call if he ever runs into trouble.

Kan leaves relieved. Happy, even.

He has no idea that he's just signed up for something that will threaten to unravel the life he came to campus to build.

---

## CHARACTER PROFILES

**KAN ("Kancity")**
The protagonist. A freshman, eager and a little naive, whose excitement at finally reaching campus is undercut almost immediately by an ordinary misfortune — a lost wallet — that pulls him somewhere he never intended to go. Kan is not seeking danger; danger finds him through a door he thought was harmless.

**EMK**
The serving executioner of the Viking Confraternity on campus. Outwardly measured, even paternal in his brief interaction with Kan — asking about his studies, offering help. The contrast between this warmth and the deference/fear he commands from others hints at the real weight of who he is. His kindness toward Kan reads, in hindsight, less like generosity and more like recruitment.

**THE GROUP (Viking Confraternity)**
A loose ensemble of more than seven men encountered at the meeting point. Function more as an atmosphere than individuals at this stage — pressure, threat, and casual menace embodied collectively. Individual members may be developed further as the story continues.

---

## NOTES FOR CONTINUATION

- This document is designed to be extended. As new installments arrive, add them as **Part 2**, **Part 3**, etc., under the Synopsis section, and update the Logline once the full arc (and stakes) are clearer.
- Consider adding a **Themes** section once more of the story is available (e.g., loss of innocence, the illusion of small kindnesses, how institutions of fear recruit through ordinary vulnerabilities).
- A **Timeline** section may be useful later if the story spans months/years, to keep the treatment's chronology clear for whoever adapts it.
